gap: No result ChatGPT got states a measured figure for any travel converter. The only named measurement found is from The Gadgeteer (Garry Kolb, 2019-11-04): a BESTEK 220V-to-110V converter (200 W rated, 250 W max) raised room noise from 28–31 dB to about 36 dB at one foot, because its cooling fan runs as soon as the unit is switched on, even with nothing plugged in.
standout_why: I opened cabinandcarry.com (no measurements and no named products with figures). I tried digitalcameraworld.com's Ceptics review, which is the only rival that tested a product, but the page returned only its title and the inkl mirror returned 403. Search excerpts of it show hands-on impressions and an RRP of about $50, with no measured numbers. travelpowerpro.com failed with a certificate error. The other results are manuals, glossary or explainer pages, or retailer pages (manuals.plus, AAA, momax, globalplugs, doace, plugvoltage, voltwander, walmart). None of the pages I could read gives a measured noise, heat or voltage figure for a converter. Outside ChatGPT's results, This Old House (updated 2026-06-10) names the BESTEK 250 W as best overall but reports only that some customers called the fan loud, with no measurement.
decides: It doesn't change which converter to buy. It adds one tested caution: the BESTEK-style fan-cooled converter can be heard at about 36 dB in a quiet room, so shoppers who will charge things overnight by the bed should expect the noise. The same reviewer also found that anything with a heating element trips the unit's shutdown. That confirms ChatGPT's own warning that these 200–250 W converters suit chargers, laptops and cameras, not hair tools. No reviewer measured output voltage, heat or noise for the TESSAN TC03, Ceptics or Foval, so they can't be compared against each other on measurements.

findings.product: BESTEK Universal Travel Adapter (220V-to-110V converter, 200 W rated / 250 W max)
findings.label: Fan noise with converter switched on
findings.value: about 36 dB average at about 1 ft (28–31 dB with it off)
findings.source_title: BESTEK Universal Travel Adapter review - The Gadgeteer
findings.note: Garry Kolb, published 2019-11-04. Measured with a phone decibel meter about a foot from the unit. Quote: 'an internal cooling fan also turns on, even with nothing plugged in'; '36 dB ... is definitely something you can hear in a quiet room'; 'from across the stateroom, it was barely audible'. The review gives no model number. The specs list 90–265 V AC input, 110 V AC output and 200 W rated / 250 W max, so it may not be the exact listing on our page.

findings.product: BESTEK Universal Travel Adapter (220V-to-110V converter, 200 W rated / 250 W max)

unsourced: Output voltage, peak voltage or waveform (oscilloscope) for the TESSAN TC03, BESTEK 250W, Ceptics 200W or Foval, measured by a named reviewer or lab. Searched for teardowns (EEVblog, Big Clive), oscilloscope tests, and RTINGS-style labs and found none.
